rounds.text: Vedant Asset Ltd demonstrates exceptional top-line and bottom-line momentum, evidenced by a compounded sales growth of 36% over 5 years [E14] and a striking 82% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E19]. This aggressive fundamental expansion is further confirmed by a rules-based screen score of 74 out of 100, driven by year-over-year sales surging by 87% and net profit jumping by 50% [E57, E58, E60]. The company operates in a supportive macro environment, as the Financial Services sector is in a strong tailwind with a score of +0.84, comfortably outperforming sector median sales growth of 14.1% [E68, E70]. Balance sheet risk is virtually nonexistent because the company is almost debt-free with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x and flat borrowings of zero [E33, E34], complemented by a significant reduction in capital-work-in-progress that indicates new capacity is coming online [E35]. Furthermore, technical strength is undisputed, with the stock holding a relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500, a 12-month price return of 71.1%, and a price positioned securely above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E43, E44, E45]. Conceded: [E38].

Vedant Asset Ltd trades at an unjustifiably rich valuation, with a trailing P/E of 56.1x and a price-to-book ratio of 3.70x, while paying a 0.00% dividend yield [E1, E2, E4]. The discounted cash flow model explicitly flags the stock as overvalued by 40.0%, pegging intrinsic value at Rs 58 against a market price of Rs 81.3 [E38, E39]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF indicates that today's market price demands a lofty 22.5% earnings growth rate, surpassing the base case assumption of 18.0% and signaling that future execution is already aggressively priced in [E40]. Underlying operational efficiency fails to justify these multiples, evidenced by a low return on equity of 5.27% alongside a depressed return on assets of 4.47%, both lagging sector benchmarks significantly [E8, E9]. Compounding these fundamental drags, the stock exhibits extreme annualised volatility of 70.9% and a devastating historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -81.3%, exposing investors to severe downside risks [E46, E47].
